title: Marie Curie: A Life for Science
summary: She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize, and the only person to win it in two different sciences.
paragraphs: Maria Sklodowska was born in Warsaw, Poland, in 1867. She was the youngest of five children. Her parents were both teachers, and they taught their children to love learning. Maria was a brilliant student, but at that time women were not allowed to study at university in Poland.

Maria did not give up. She worked for several years as a private teacher and saved her money. She also helped to pay for her older sister's studies in Paris. In 1891, when she was twenty-four, Maria finally moved to Paris herself and started studying physics and mathematics at the famous Sorbonne university. In France she used the name Marie.
Life in Paris was hard. Marie had very little money. She lived in a small cold room and sometimes forgot to eat because she was so busy studying. But she finished her studies at the top of her class.

In 1894 she met Pierre Curie, a French scientist. They shared the same passion for science, and a year later they got married. Together they began to study a strange kind of energy that came from certain rocks. Marie called it “radioactivity”. Working in a small, poorly equipped building, the couple discovered two new chemical elements. Marie named one of them polonium, after her home country.

In 1903, Marie and Pierre won the Nobel Prize in Physics, together with another scientist. Marie was the first woman ever to receive the prize. But only three years later, tragedy came. Pierre was killed in a street accident in Paris. Marie was left alone with their two young daughters.

Although she was heartbroken, Marie continued their work. She took Pierre's job at the university and became the first woman professor there. In 1911, she won a second Nobel Prize, this time in Chemistry. She is still the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences.

During the First World War, Marie used her knowledge to help soldiers. She developed small X-ray machines that could be driven to the battlefield in cars. These machines helped doctors find bullets and broken bones, and they saved many lives.

At that time, nobody understood that radioactivity was dangerous. Marie often carried radioactive materials in her pockets. After many years of working with them, she became seriously ill, and she died in 1934. Her notebooks are still so radioactive today that they are kept in special boxes. Marie Curie changed science forever, and she showed the world what women could achieve.

questions.question: Why did Maria leave Poland to study?
options: Her parents wanted her to live in France
Women could not study at university in Poland
She did not like Polish schools
She won a prize to study abroad
questions.explanation: At that time women were not allowed to study at university in Poland.

questions.question: How did Marie choose the name polonium?
questions.explanation: She named the element polonium after her home country.

questions.question: What happened in 1906, three years after the first prize?
questions.explanation: Three years after 1903, Pierre was killed in a street accident.

questions.question: How did Marie help during the First World War?
options: She worked as a nurse in Poland
She built small X-ray machines that could travel to the battlefield
She gave her prize money to soldiers
questions.explanation: She developed small X-ray machines in cars that helped doctors find bullets and broken bones.

questions.question: Why are Marie's notebooks kept in special boxes?
options: They are very old and weak
They are worth a lot of money
questions.explanation: Her notebooks are still radioactive today, so they are kept in special boxes.

grammar.explanation: We use the past passive when we focus on what happened to someone, not who did it.
grammar.example: Pierre was killed in a street accident in Paris.

exercise.question: Choose the correct passive sentence.
options: Maria was born in Warsaw in 1867.
Maria is born in Warsaw in 1867.
Maria was borned in Warsaw in 1867.

grammar.explanation: Although joins two ideas that seem to go against each other.
grammar.example: Although she was heartbroken, Marie continued their work.

exercise.question: Choose the best word: ___ she had little money, she finished at the top of her class.
exercise.explanation: Having little money and doing very well is a contrast, so we use although.
